en: I worship the state of Rāmacandra, which is the body of the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā) established by the Mahāvākyas, and which is liberation without the physical body (vikalevara-kaivalya).
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Worshipful Ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise [you] with hymns.
May we attain the lifespan ordained by the gods.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
Hariḥ Oṃ.

Then the Blessed Lord Brahmā said: "We shall explain the supreme secret Upaniṣad of direct experience. This most secret of secrets must not be taught to one who is ordinary; it should be taught to one who is sattvic, introverted, and desirous of learning. Then...

Having withdrawn the two eyes of knowledge and ignorance regarding the bondage and liberation of saṃsāra, and having discerned that ignorance is the seer of the darkness within the egg of the world, one realizes that this darkness is indeed the phenomenal expansion of the body, extending from Brahmā down to the immovable, consisting of the infinite and entire multitude of unborn eggs of worlds.
The world is characterized by the performance of ritual actions according to desire as proclaimed by the entirety of the Vedas;

yet this is not the Self, which is darkness. For knowledge is the solar orb of light to be grasped from another section [of the Veda], and nothing else; that sun is Brahman, as established through the *ajapā* [mantra].

"I am that Haṃsa. Having thus attained [the state] by means of the prāṇa and apāna breaths moving in reverse and forward order, and having long since obtained it, when one meditates upon the threefold Brahman within the Self, the Supreme Self— being Existence, Consciousness, and Bliss— manifests.
Because it is suffused and filled by the thousand-rayed sun, it is as if an ocean filled to its shores;
yet this is not meditative absorption (*samādhi*), nor is this the perfection of yoga (*yoga-siddhi*), nor is this the dissolution of the mind (*manolaya*).
That is oneness with Brahman—of the nature of the sun, beyond darkness.
Having discerned all forms and having created names, the Wise One remains calling them forth.
The Ordainer proclaimed him in the beginning; Śakra, the wise one, [proclaimed him] in the four quarters. Knowing him alone, one becomes immortal here; no other path for going exists.

By means of sacrifice, the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first dharmas. Those great ones attained the heights of heaven, where the ancient Sādhya gods abide. I am that Arka, the supreme light; I am Śiva, whose light is the Arka.

I am the light of the Self, the pure, the essence of all lights, Om! Whoever studies this Atharvaśiras, studying it in the morning, destroys the sin committed during the night; studying it in the evening, he destroys the sin committed during the day.
By reciting this in the evening and in the morning, one who is sinful becomes sinless;
by reciting it at midday while facing the sun,
one is liberated from the five great sins and minor offenses.
One obtains the merit of studying all the Vedas to their completion;
one attains union with the glorious Mahāviṣṇu—thus ends the Upaniṣad.
Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O worshipful ones. With firm limbs and bodies, may we praise you.
May we attain the life-span ordained by the gods.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace! Hariḥ Oṃ Tatsat.
Thus ends the Mahāvākya Upaniṣad.
